explanation: Neuroevolution corresponds to biological evolution: Neuroevolution algorithm is a method of optimizing artificial neural networks by simulating the evolution of biological neural networks; biological evolution refers to the genetic and morphological changes that occur in organisms during the long process of evolution. Both describe the process of evolution.

Artificial neural networks correspond to organisms: Artificial neural networks are a computational model that simulates the structure and function of biological neural networks; organisms are concrete entities in the process of biological evolution. Both involve the structure and function of biological neural networks.

background.source: Neuroevolutionary algorithms have revolutionized the way we approach artificial intelligence. One of the most significant breakthroughs in this area has been the promoter-based genetic algorithm (PBGA). Developed by F. Bellas and R.J. Duro at the University of Coruña in Spain, PBGA has enabled variable-sized feedforward artificial neural networks (ANNs) to be evolved. ANNs were previously restricted in size, but thanks to PBGA, the size of ANNs can be dynamically adjusted to best suit the particular task at hand. The key to PBGA is the use of a gene promoter that acts as an on/off switch for each block of the ANN. This transcriptional response ensures that only the most useful neural networks are expressed, leading to more efficient and effective AI.
background.target: Evolution is a fascinating concept in biology where heritable characteristics of biological populations undergo constant change over successive generations leading to biodiversity at every level of biological organization. The expressions of genes passed down from parents to offspring during reproduction result in variation within a given population due to genetic mutation and recombination. With evolutionary processes such as natural selection and genetic drift, certain characteristics become common or rare within a population, leading to a change in heritable characteristics over time. This theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed by Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace in the mid-19th century and studied by evolutionary biologists to understand the diverse aspects and influences of evolution. Evolutionary discoveries have not only influenced the development of biology but also various other scientific and industrial fields including medicine, agriculture, and computer science.
